page.title: Quicksort
page.desc: Tony Hoare's 1959 divide-and-conquer sort: pick a pivot, partition, recurse. O(n log n) on average, O(n²) worst case, in place and cache-friendly.
page.intro: Tony Hoare's 1959 divide-and-conquer sort: pick a pivot, partition, recurse. O(n log n) on average, O(n²) worst case, in place and cache-friendly.

synapses.text: Everything smaller goes left, larger right; the pivot is then in its final place and both sides are sorted recursively.
Sorted input with a first-element pivot gives the quadratic case; median-of-three or random pivots avoid it, and introsort falls back to heapsort.

parent.desc: Putting things in order; comparison sorts cannot beat Ω(n log n), and the interesting differences are stability, memory and behaviour on real data.
